verifications.claim: As of April 2026, NASA has not yet announced the specific crewmembers for the Artemis III mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the Artemis III crew will be revealed in the near future'; R3: 'We don't yet know who will fly on Artemis 3; NASA has not announced the crewmembers.'; R2: 'As of April 2026, NASA had not finalized...' (context post-Artemis II in 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm no announcement as of April 2026 or around that time.

verifications.claim: Artemis III mission is currently planned for a 2027 launch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'targeted launch in mid-2027'; 'NASA expects Artemis III to launch in mid-2027'; R3: 'scheduled to launch in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements of 2027 launch plan across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis III mission is planned to test docking in low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'conduct rendezvous and docking tests in low Earth orbit'; 'Mission planners are considering both low Earth orbit (LEO) and high Earth orbit (HEO)'; R3: 'practice rendezvous and docking operations in Earth orbit'; R4: 'Artemis III mission in low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Earth orbit docking test, with R2 and R4 specifying low Earth orbit as planned or considered primary.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will fly on a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'launch aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R3: 'launch atop a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R4: 'launch in Orion on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Unanimous direct support from all relevant sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis III will rendezvous with a commercial lunar lander (Starship or Blue Moon).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'rendezvous in Earth orbit with one or both commercially developed Human Landing System (HLS) vehicles—SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon'; R3: 'meet up with Starship and/or Blue Moon'; R4: 'test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match naming Starship/Blue Moon as rendezvous targets.

verifications.claim: Artemis III mission will focus on testing rendezvous and docking capabilities between the Orion spacecraft and human landing systems in Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test rendezvous and docking operations'; 'test the docking of the Orion capsule with at least one... lunar landers'; R3: 'practice rendezvous and docking operations in Earth orbit... Orion and one or both of the private landers'; R4: 'test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Precise description matches source content directly.

verifications.claim: NASA named 18 astronauts in 2020 involved in previous Artemis training exercises.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA names 18 astronauts for Artemis moon missions' (Dec 2020); 'Eighteen astronauts have been selected... to begin training for upcoming Artemis missions'
verifications.reasoning: Naming 18 in 2020 is correct, but they were selected 'to begin training for upcoming' missions, not 'involved in previous' exercises, directly contradicting 'previous'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the immediate prior mission to Artemis III.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis program ← Artemis II Artemis IV →'; R3: 'Artemis 3 is the third scheduled flight... after... Artemis 2'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly sequence Artemis II immediately before III.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will orbit the Moon in early 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis 2, which could launch as soon as April 1, 2026'; 'on a roughly 10-day trip around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states early 2026 lunar orbit plan; R2 context post-Artemis II aligns.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'four astronauts — NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency'

verifications.claim: Artemis III is for testing the SpaceX Starship or Blue Moon lander with the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) space suits.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test one or both... Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon...'; 'may also include evaluation of the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) space suit'; 'test the new spacesuits that will be used on the Moon, the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm testing landers (Starship/Blue Moon) and separately testing AxEMU suits, but not explicitly 'with' suits as part of lander testing; broader support but less precise linkage.
